info.bio:
John Prine (Maywood, Illinois, 10 de octubre de 1946) es un cantautor de country y folk estadounidense con un amplio éxito, tanto de crítica como de público, desde la década de 1970.

Sus padres fueron William Prine y Verna Hamm. Su abuelo había sido guitarrista de Merle Travis y Prine se inició como guitarrista a los catorce años. Durante cinco años trabajó como cartero, e hizo el servicio militar antes de comenzar su carrera musical en Chicago.

scenes.name: Cantautores de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: James Taylor se convierte, misteriosamente, en el prototipo del cantautor de los setenta; Carole King, Carly Simon y Don McLean, sobrevalorados. Las innovaciones llegan del oeste: Randy Newman y sus viñetas urbanas con fusión de estilos populares, Shawn Phillips, J.J. Cale y su estilo «laid-back», Gram Parsons, Emmylou Harris, Roger McGuinn, Jackson Browne (Late For The Sky) y, sobre todo, Tom Waits, discípulo de Beefheart y cronista de marginados (Swordfishtrombones, Rain Dogs). Excéntricos como Todd Rundgren y Annette Peacock; en Gran Bretaña, Peter Hammill, Anthony Moore, Richard Thompson, Robert Calvert, John Cale, Kevin Coyne, Elton John y los ex Beatles. El realismo de Bruce Springsteen, verdadero heredero de Woody Guthrie y del blues, y la escuela italiana de cantautores (De André, Guccini, Battisti, Sorrenti).

podcast.title: Eight Austin City Limits Appearances (1978-2002)
podcast.body: John Prine performed on Austin City Limits a total of eight times, with his first appearance in 1978 and another notable one in 2002 where he sang "Angel from Montgomery" with Bonnie Raitt. "One Prine was on Austin City Limits eight times, the first time being in 1978."

podcast.title: Austin City Limits Hall of Fame Induction (2024)
podcast.body: In January 2024, John Prine was inducted into the Austin City Limits Hall of Fame during its ninth annual ceremony. Actor Ethan Hawke delivered the induction speech, praising Prine as a singer-songwriter who pursued excellence and truth over fame. "In January 2024, Austin City Limits held its ninth annual Hall of Fame ceremony and John Prine was inducted into that Hall of Fame."

podcast.title: "Mark Twain of American Songwriting"
podcast.body: In a 2017 Rolling Stone article, Patrick Doyle referred to John Prine as "the Mark Twain of American Songwriting" due to his exceptional storytelling ability. His music offered reassurance and resonated with those seeking comfort in life's bigger problems, making him a perfect fit for Austin City Limits despite his hard-to-categorize blend of country, folk, and blues. "In a Rolling Stone article about John Prine's life that was published in 2017, Patrick Doyle referred to Prine as the Mark Twain of American Songwriting."

podcast.title: Critical Success
podcast.body: John Prine is mentioned as a "critical success" among singer-songwriters sampled by critic Robert Hillburn in 1973. He was featured in Hillburn's 1973 Los Angeles Times article alongside Bruce Springsteen and Danny O'Keefe. "Hillburn had sampled like popular favorites, like John Denver, those who had just had breakthrough hits like O'Keefe, a couple of critical successes like Prine, and then three quote unknowns."

podcast.title: Example of "Stoner" Music
podcast.body: Neil Bogart cited John Prine as an artist whose music catered to "heavy stoners" who would "sit there and drink your bottle of beer and get into that shit." This contrasted with the mood-setting, romantic music he envisioned for Donna Summer. "There's a music for the heavy stoners that sit there and listen to some dynamite people, John Prine."

podcast.title: Mailman as Lyricist
podcast.body: Before his musical career took off, John Prine worked as a mailman. He would use the time walking his mail route to think through his lyrics, indicating a deep engagement with his songwriting process even during his day job. "Now back then, Prine was a male man. And so he would just use that time when he was out walking his route to think through his lyrics."

podcast.title: Perspective in Songwriting
podcast.body: John Prine demonstrated a unique empathy in his songwriting, notably with "Angel from Montgomery," written at age 25 from the perspective of a middle-aged woman feeling trapped and old. Bonnie Raitt, a young feminist at the time, deeply resonated with this song's portrayal of a woman in a thankless marriage, highlighting Prine's ability to transcend his own experiences. "It's a song written by a 25 year old man in 70 or 71 whenever he actually wrote it. From the perspective of a middle-aged woman who feels old and it works, Bonnie said that as a young feminist that there was something about a song written by a man from the perspective of a woman who was in kind of a, what seemed like a thankless marriage that really resonated with her."

podcast.body: The transcript notes the significant loss felt by John Prine's passing during the COVID pandemic, highlighting his immense value as a songwriter. "And John Prine's loss, that's still hurt."
